reuse.why: Most bulk actions share the new category selector and existing budget infrastructure, but copyPreviousMonth independently implements the same eligibility policy.

duplication.why: The selector removes repeated category queries, but eligibility remains duplicated across SQL and TypeScript and the new action repeats the income-mode guard.

placement.why: Selection and budget operations remain in actions.ts, with method registration and undo wrapping in app.ts following existing layering.

scope.why: The changes are confined to the requested bulk-budget policies, new action, method registration, and relevant tests.

maintainability.why: The shared selector improves ownership, but maintaining a separate eligibility implementation for copying makes future policy changes require coordinated edits.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth uses getBudgetData and local exclusions instead of the shared getCategoriesForBulkAction policy.

disguised_duplication.where: actions.ts expresses hidden, saved-template, and fixed-group eligibility as SQL predicates in getCategoriesForBulkAction and as projected fields plus TypeScript conditions in getBudgetData/copyPreviousMonth.

abstraction_drift.where: getCategoriesForBulkAction gains includeHiddenCategories and its conditional SQL exclusion; copyPreviousMonth retains a separate policy implementation outside that helper.
